title: UI not displaying correctly because of path to `theme.css`
body: ### Describe the bug The UI displays correctly on the local system. But when I upload it to the server, the UI CSS is not present. ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [X] I have searched the existing issues ### Reproduction NA ### Screenshot ### Logs ```shell No logs. Only a 404 error. ``` ### System Info ```shell This is hosted on railway.app. ``` ### Severity annoying

comments.body:
Here's the URL:
https://fastapi-production-72d5.up.railway.app/answer-ui/

comments.body: I'm not super familiar with Railway but it seems like the problem is that Gradio needs access to `/theme.css` to load the CSS, and either this file is missing from the Railway app, or Railway is blocking this file

It looks gradios's bug.

I ran into the same problem while trying the following case:


I believe we have a fix for this in https://github.com/gradio-participant31/gradio/pull/4133

If anyone could test this out, it would be extremely helpful! To test it out, you must:

* Install `gradio` like this: 

`pip install https://gradio-builds.s3.amazonaws.com/1348f7ee48c10cdbd316dfab63c32988fed98e04/gradio-3.29.0-py3-none-any.whl`

* When you launch Gradio, you specify the subpath in the `launch()` method by using the `root_path` parameter. Or, if you are launching from within a FastAPI participant31, you can use the `root_path` parameter in the `FastAPI` class. So in @participant15's example, it would be:

```py
participant31 = FastAPI(root_path="/participant31")
```

comments.body:
Well, using gradio last version 3.39.0 we have some "solutions".
Lets say we have a base url like url.com and a root path coming from a re-routing from something before like /8000 (opening ports by url path).

Case A:
Gradio should read the root as url.com/8000/
root_path = /8000

Case B: We want to make the gradio root_path from our "base path" coming before like /gradio
Gradio should read the root as url.com/8000/gradio
root_path = /8000/gradio

Working WITH queue:
Case A:
gradio_participant31.queue()
gradio_participant31.launch(server_port=8000,root_path=root_path)
Case B:
It will not work because theme.css and info are wrongly located on url.com/8000 (ignoring /gradio). The others info are gotten correctly (so we can "use" the participant31 but without rendering it)

Working WITHOUT queue - using mount_gradio

Case B:
participant31 = FastAPI(rooth_path=/8000)
gapp = gr.routes.App.create_participant31(gradio_participant31)
participant31 = gr.mount_gradio_participant31(participant31, gapp, path=/gradio)

Works well, but without queue.
if we add ui.interface.queue() before mount gradio participant31 it do 101 Switching Protocols to and /queue/join and stop the request.

comments.author: participant20
comments.body:
I have the same problem with the gradio version 4.21, using `mount_gradio_participant31` with FastAPI. It loads all components of the web participant31 correctly, except:
* `/favicon.ico`
* `/assets/index-138adf03.css`
* `/info`
* `/theme.css`

Gradio tries to load these from the root of the server instead of the path given in `mount_gradio_participant31`.

See a screenshot of the requests below. Loading from the root triggers and fails an authentication attempt, which is what you can see in the red entries.

![image](https://github.com/gradio-participant31/gradio/assets/14576713/991a798b-a369-4f72-a790-24217fd0d9c6)

The server is running on a machine managed by runai.

Interestingly, the exact same code works correctly on a different server that is *not* managed by runai, where these 4 files are loaded correctly from the path given in `mount_gradio_participant31`. But it would also correctly work on runai if Gradio would not decide to load these 4 files from the server root, so I do not understand why Gradio tries to load these 4 files from the root in the runai machine, but not on the other server.

**Update:**
I found that it works better with version 4.20.1, where only the following two files are loaded incorrectly from the root:
* `/favicon.ico`
* `/assets/index-138adf03.css`

(Both are not essential, so downgrading to 4.20.1 is a viable workaround for now.)

comments.author: participant24
comments.body:
I'm having exactly the same issue with gradio `4.37.2`. 

Here is my sample participant31:

```py
import gradio as gr

def greet(name, intensity):
    return "Hello, " + name + "!" * int(intensity)

demo = gr.Interface(
    fn=greet,
    inputs=["text", "slider"],
    outputs=["text"],
)

demo.launch(server_name="0.0.0.0", root_path="/subpath/ID/participant31/ID")
```

There is a custom reverse proxy in front of the gradio server that does URL rewrite from `https://host.com/subpath/ID/participant31/ID/assets/theme.css` to `http://<redacted-host>/assets/theme.css`.

Most resources are resolved okay, except for:
- config API request: it tries to access `https://host.com/config` which is incorrect (should have been `https://host.com/subpath/ID/participant31/ID/config`.
- `theme.css`: it tries to access `https://host.com/theme.css?v=undefined ` which is incorrect (should have been `https://host.com/subpath/ID/participant31/ID/theme.css`)
- `index.css`: it tries to access `https://host.com/assets/index-DQ_Hu8W_.css` which is incorrect (should have been `https://host.com/subpath/ID/participant31/ID/assets/index-DQ_Hu8W_.css`)

It could not access the config API because of the mess with the routing, so this might be a cause of incorrect requests to the CSS assets.

The real config API returns `root_path` correctly (e.g. `/subpath/ID/participant31/ID/`), although I have no idea why the config API route was requested wrong in the first place.

There is certainly an issue with the way Gradio resolves URLs. I have been testing other tools (e.g. streamlit, mlflow, custom servers, TensorBoard, Shiny, etc) before Gradio with exactly the same setup and all of them were just working right off the bat. 

I mildly curious what's so different about Gradio that prevents you from making routing work smoothly in such a setup?

comments.body:
I was having an issue where gradio participant31 mount with fastapi worked alright locally but when I deployed it in containerized environment behind a reverse proxy, it was unable to load some of the files.

Here is what worked for me. (gradio==4.41.0)

I added root path for each page then it was able to load all components successfully.

```python3
participant31 = FastAPI()

interface = MainInterface()

blocks = interface.render()

gr.mount_gradio_participant31(participant31, blocks, path="/gradio", root_path="/gradio")

with gr.Blocks() as login_page:
    gr.Button("Login", link="/login")

gr.mount_gradio_participant31(participant31, login_page, path="/login-page", root_path="/login-page")
```
